## introduction

Processing videos are costly because of the large amount of images it contains.
But luckily, thanks to video compression algorithm
(as explained in much better details in [this post](https://jdhao.github.io/2021/12/25/ffmpeg-extract-key-frame-video/))
we can use `ffmpeg` to quickly get out the keyframes (aka I-frames).

::: {#fig-demo}
![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:720/format:webp/1*sA0nxYotnQAkBYUiydUwXQ.jpeg){.preview-image}

Visualizing i-frames in a sequence of video frames[^demo-image-note]
:::

I-frames are basically the highest quality images in a video. The frames
surrounding them only stores the "differences" w.r.t. the I-frames.

[^demo-image-note]: image [source](https://medium.com/@publiciscommerce/extracting-i-frames-keyframes-from-a-video-using-ffmpeg-cb7f2ae3add1)

## I-frames Extraction
```
ffmpeg -skip_frame nokey -i your_video.mp4 \
    -vsync 0 -frame_pts true output/dir/iframe_%d.jpg
```

* `skip_frame` tells the decoder to process only keyframes
* `-vsync 0` preserves timestamps
* `-frame_pts` set the output file's `%d` to each keyframe's presentation timestamp (PTS)
    * so to compute the actual timestamp, for example `iframe_75.jpg` with a fps of 30, the iframe's timestamp would be 2.50 seconds
    * you can read more about it [here](https://superuser.com/a/1421195) and [here](https://stackoverflow.com/a/56999262)

## using a filter to select "Contextual Scene Change"
no need for OpenCV, ffmpeg can do this too with a little filter action:
```
ffmpeg -i your_video.mp4 \
    -vf "select='gt(scene,0.3)'"
    -vsync 0 -frame_pts true output/dir/kframe_%d.jpg
```

* the value for `scene` should be a float between 0 and 1 and it measures the pixel level difference between two frames. So here our threshold is 30%

:::{.callout-tip}
## i-frames already have "Contextual Scene Changing" frames
from personal testing, there are a lot more i-frames than there are "Contextual Scene Changing" frames
but they also include them. So there are no need to run both.

If your want to save downstream processing time, then filter for "Contextual Scene Changing" Frames.
Otherwise, just use i-frames to be as inclusive as possible!
:::
